title: Gas-Syringe Kinetics with Marble Chips
learningGoal: Assemble a safe expanding gas-collection path, use teacher-approved acid volume/concentration and marble-mass settings, collect a synchronized carbon-dioxide time series, distinguish simulator-generated series from student measurements, calculate an initial rate, and identify limits on the evidence.

actions.label: Verify the nonblocked expanding gas path

parameters.note: Before reactant contact, verify every connection is present, tubing is not kinked, the recorded baseline still stands, and the syringe plunger can expand freely. Reject a missing connection separately from a blocked pressure hazard; exact locking geometry remains teacher-confirmed.

prerequisites.label: The gas syringe baseline is recorded.

stateChanges: Record the leak check, zero check, and expanding pressure-relief path.

invalidCases.when: A stopper, tube, or syringe connection is missing or leaking.
invalidCases.message: The apparatus cannot provide valid carbon-dioxide volume evidence.
invalidCases.recovery: Reconnect the missing component and repeat the leak check.

invalidCases.when: The tubing is kinked or the syringe plunger cannot move.
invalidCases.message: The apparatus could build pressure instead of expanding safely.
invalidCases.recovery: Stop and restore the approved expanding or vented path before adding reactants.

invalidCases.when: the tubing is kinked, the plunger cannot expand, or a rigid closed volume would trap generated gas
invalidCases.message: Do not initiate gas generation against a blocked or non-expanding path.
invalidCases.recovery: Keep reactants separated, open or reconfigure the collection path, then repeat the path and baseline checks.

feedback.success: Gas path, plunger travel, and zero are checked.
feedback.invalid: Record the gas syringe baseline before leak-checking the train.

interaction.successCue: Gas path and baseline check recorded.
interaction.invalidCue: Record the connection, baseline, plunger-travel and pressure-relief checks.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Record the leak, baseline and pressure-relief checks for the collection train.

actions.label: Arm the timer and define first contact as time zero

parameters.note: Arm the timer before the reactants meet. The first physical contact of the weighed marble with acid is the reaction-start and timer-start event; the first series row is the configured time-zero evidence. Exact trigger or locking geometry remains teacher-confirmed.

prerequisites.label: The marble mass is recorded while reactants remain separate.
The nonblocked expanding gas path is verified.

stateChanges: The timer is armed and the approved first-contact time-zero rule is recorded while reactants remain separate.

invalidCases.when: Timing begins after the defined reactant-contact event.
invalidCases.message: A delayed time zero biases the early-rate evidence.
invalidCases.recovery: Use fresh configured reactants and repeat the run with timing synchronized to the approved contact event.

feedback.success: Reaction contact, gas collection, and time zero synchronized.
feedback.invalid: Record all controlled quantities before initiating the reaction.

interaction.accessibleLabel: Record the approved contact-defined time-zero rule before initiating the reaction.
interaction.successCue: The timer is armed before contact.
interaction.invalidCue: Define and arm the time-zero rule before allowing reactant contact.

actions.label: Initiate the reaction by adding the weighed marble to acid

parameters.note: Transfer the exact {{presentation.marbleTarget}} balance reading into {{presentation.acidAmount}} of acid. This depletes the marble-chip stock only at transfer; it does not use a configured runtime mass fallback.

interaction.successCue: The marble chips are in the acid; the reaction has started.
interaction.invalidCue: Tip the weighed marble chips into the open reaction flask.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Add the weighed marble chips to the acid in the reaction flask.

prerequisites.label: The gas path and baseline are checked.
The timer is armed and first contact is defined as time zero.

stateChanges: The first marble-acid contact starts the reaction and timer at the same defined time-zero event.

invalidCases.when: Reactants meet before the train is connected, zeroed and leak-checked.
invalidCases.message: Carbon dioxide produced before the path is verified is lost.
invalidCases.recovery: Keep the failed-run record and repeat with fresh reactants after verifying the train.

invalidCases.message: Solid cannot be added through a seated delivery stopper.
invalidCases.recovery: Add the chips to the open flask, then seal through the approved path.

feedback.success: Marble chips added to the acid; seal the flask and start the timer now.
feedback.invalid: Measure the marble-chip mass before initiating the reaction.

actions.label: Seal the charged flask through the verified path

interaction.successCue: The stopper and delivery tube are seated in the flask.
interaction.invalidCue: Seat the delivery stopper in the reaction flask.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Seat the rubber stopper and delivery tube in the Erlenmeyer flask.

prerequisites.label: The weighed marble chips are in the acid.

stateChanges: Seat the already connected, zeroed and leak-checked delivery stopper in the charged flask, keeping the path to the freely moving syringe open.

invalidCases.when: The stoppered reaction vessel has no freely expanding or vented gas path.
invalidCases.message: Do not generate carbon dioxide in a rigid closed system.
invalidCases.recovery: Connect the gas syringe, verify that its plunger moves freely, and leak-check the complete path before sealing the flask.

invalidCases.when: The flask is sealed before the acid and the marble chips are in it.
invalidCases.message: A sealed flask cannot be charged, and sealing early loses the start of the run.
invalidCases.recovery: Charge the open flask first, then seal through the verified path.

feedback.success: The charged flask is sealed through the verified expanding path.
feedback.invalid: Add the acid and the weighed chips to the open flask before sealing it.

feedback.invalid: Synchronize reaction contact and time zero before recording the series.

interaction.successCue: Timed carbon-dioxide volumes recorded against the syringe graduations.
interaction.invalidCue: Read the gas syringe at each configured sampling time and record the paired value.
interaction.accessibleLabel: Record the timed gas syringe volumes for the guided series.

actions.label: Calculate the guided initial rate

parameters.note: The rate is derived from the recorded series over the configured secant interval. No expected value is stored: the gate is that the timed evidence exists, because a stored answer would be a fabricated measurement rather than a derivation.

prerequisites.label: The guided gas-volume series is recorded.

stateChanges: Calculate the secant slope from 0 s to 15 s and report it in mL CO2/s.

feedback.invalid: Record the guided time series before calculating its early slope.

interaction.accessibleLabel: Calculate a rate from the separately recorded raw series.
interaction.successCue: The rate is derived from the selected evidence interval.
interaction.invalidCue: Record the raw series before calculating a rate.

actions.label: Review evidence limits and repeatability

parameters.note: The displayed series is deterministic simulator output for the stated guided configuration, not a student measurement or a replicate distribution. Physical runs require approved acid settings, fresh reactants, repeated trials, documented syringe resolution, and review of leaks, plunger friction, start-time synchronization, chip-size heterogeneity, marble composition, temperature drift, and mixing. Do not infer a universal rate law or real monument lifetime from this single classroom model.

prerequisites.label: The derived rate calculation is recorded.

stateChanges: Record the simulator provenance, repeatability needs, assumptions, and excluded effects.

feedback.success: Evidence limits and repeatability needs recorded.
feedback.invalid: Calculate the guided initial rate before interpreting its limits.

interaction.accessibleLabel: Record limits of the simulator series and derived rate.
interaction.successCue: Evidence and model limits are recorded.
interaction.invalidCue: Separate raw series evidence from the rate calculation and model assumptions.

commonMistakes.when: The reaction is initiated with a blocked or rigidly closed collection path.
commonMistakes.message: Gas generation in a rigid closed system can build unsafe pressure.
commonMistakes.recovery: Stop and restore the teacher-approved freely expanding or vented path.

commonMistakes.when: The timer is started after the defined reactant-contact event.
commonMistakes.message: Late timing biases the initial-rate calculation.
commonMistakes.recovery: Repeat with fresh configured reactants and synchronize timing to the defined contact event.

commonMistakes.when: The deterministic simulator series is described as student-measured replicate data.
commonMistakes.message: The guided series has no experimental scatter and cannot establish repeatability.
commonMistakes.recovery: Label simulator-generated data explicitly and use approved physical repeats for experimental variability.
